frame: One adult in plain clothes stands whole-figure in side view on a flat ground line, one arm pointing, beside a single plain wooden stool on the same line, a plain low wall behind, same figure size on the page. Only the place of the stool changes: right at the adult's feet, or far along the line.
sentence_nl: Mijn tas staat hier, maar jouw tas staat daar.
sentence_en: My bag is here, but your bag is there.

frame: A small plain house seen from the front, with a pitched roof, one window and one shut door, stands on a flat ground line; its front wall is drawn as a cutaway so the one room shows. One adult in plain clothes, same size in every drawing. Only the place of the adult changes: in the room or on the ground in front.
sentence_nl: Ik ben binnen, maar mijn vriend is buiten.
sentence_en: I am inside, but my friend is outside.

frame: A plain wooden table with two plain chairs seen from the side, one cup on the table for each seated adult, a plain wall behind, same table and chairs on the page. Only the number of people seated changes: two adults, or one.
sentence_nl: Wij eten samen, maar hij eet alleen.
sentence_en: We eat together, but he eats alone.

frame: Two children of the same height stand side by side, whole-figure, facing the viewer, on a flat ground line with a plain wall behind. Each has one hand raised at shoulder height. Only what the children hold changes: a plain balloon on a string in the hands.
sentence_nl: Alleen Eva heeft een ballon, maar Tom wil ook een ballon.
sentence_en: Only Eva has a balloon, but Tom wants a balloon too.

frame: One plain table lamp with a round shade stands on a small plain table, seen from the front, its cord running down to the floor, a plain wall behind, same size on the page. Only the lamp changes: shining or not shining.
sentence_nl: In de keuken is het licht aan, maar in de gang is het uit.
sentence_en: In the kitchen the light is on, but in the hall it is off.

frame: A small plain house with its front wall cut away stands at the left edge on a flat ground line; a plain road runs from its door to the right edge. The room holds a plain sofa and an empty wall hook. One adult in plain clothes with a plain shoulder bag, same size in every drawing. Only the place of the adult changes: in the room, or on the road.
sentence_nl: Ik ben thuis, maar mijn man is onderweg.
sentence_en: I am at home, but my husband is on the way.

frame: One plain flat tray lies on a plain wooden table seen from the front, a plain wall behind, same size on the page. Only the number of whole round apples lying on the tray changes.
sentence_nl: Ik heb veel appels, maar jij hebt weinig appels.
sentence_en: I have a lot of apples, but you have few apples.

frame: Three adults in plain clothes sit side by side at one long plain table seen from the front, hands resting on the table, a plain wall behind, same figures and table size on the page. Only the number of plain cups on the table changes: three, or seven.
sentence_nl: Wij hebben genoeg kopjes, maar zij hebben te veel kopjes.
sentence_en: We have enough cups, but they have too many cups.

frame: One plain drinking glass stands on a plain table seen from the front, a plain jug beside it, a plain wall behind, same sizes on the page. Only the water level in the glass changes, and whether the jug is still pouring.
sentence_nl: Het eerste glas is helemaal vol, het tweede glas is bijna vol en het derde glas heeft maar een beetje water.
sentence_en: The first glass is completely full, the second glass is almost full and the third glass has only a little water.

frame: A low plain brick wall stands on a flat ground line, seen from the side, with one adult in plain clothes standing upright beside it holding one trowel, a plain low sky behind, same size in every drawing. Only the wall changes: complete with a flat top and no bricks left, or half built with a stepped top and a brick pile beside it.
sentence_nl: Deze muur is af, maar met die muur is hij nog bezig.
sentence_en: This wall is finished, but he is still busy with that wall.

frame: Skipped set: the days relative to today.
sentence_nl: Gisteren was het droog, vandaag regent het en morgen schijnt de zon.
sentence_en: Yesterday was dry, today it rains and tomorrow the sun shines.

sentence_nl: Ik werk nu, maar ik rust straks uit.
sentence_en: I am working now, but I will rest later.

sentence_nl: Hij is altijd op tijd, maar zij is nooit op tijd.
sentence_en: He is always on time, but she is never on time.

sentence_nl: Ik fiets vaak, mijn broer fietst zelden en mijn zus fietst soms.
sentence_en: I cycle often, my brother rarely cycles and my sister sometimes cycles.

sentence_nl: Ik ben al klaar, maar jij bent nog bezig.
sentence_en: I am already done, but you are still busy.

sentence_nl: Eerst eten wij, daarna gaan wij wandelen.
sentence_en: First we eat, afterwards we go for a walk.

sentence_nl: Misschien komt hij, maar zij komt zeker.
sentence_en: Maybe he will come, but she will certainly come.

sentence_nl: Hij komt wel, maar zij komt niet.
sentence_en: He is coming, but she is not coming.
